pages.text: Two black holes spiralling together shake spacetime: a wave passes, stretching space one way and squeezing it the other, by a strain h of 10⁻²¹ when it reaches us. The $(item)Laser Interferometer$() is an L of two long arms with a $(item)Test Mass$() at each end: a laser split between the arms comes back to interfere, and a wave changes the pattern.

Four noises hide the wave. $(thing)Shot noise$(), the graininess of light, falls as the laser power P and the arms' finesse F rise - but $(thing)radiation pressure$(), the photons' kicks on the mirrors, grows with them. Both depend only on F√P; where they are equal is the standard quantum limit.

$(thing)Seismic noise$() falls tenfold with each isolation stage - more stages, slower to lock. Machines running nearby shake the ground; below sea level it is quieter, as at KAGRA. $(thing)Thermal noise$() in the mirrors falls as √T: cool them with your coolant.

A black hole merger, h = 10⁻²¹, needs a signal-to-noise of 8. A neutron star merger is five times fainter: only cold mirrors will do. Its record points a telescope at the $(thing)kilonova$() - where gold and platinum were made - and every detection gives a great deal of Insight. The chirp's parameters are read off by Bayesian inference: the Analyzer takes black hole records as evidence.
